newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia government to censor television.
newsitem.headline: Zambia government to censor television.

text.p: Zambia plans to censor state-run television to stop "nude activities" rubbing shoulders with religious programmes, Deputy President Godfrey Miyanda told parliament.
Local newspapers on Friday quoted Miyanda as saying the government was disturbed by the mixture of Christian and other programmes on television in a country which is legally a Christian state.
"Sometimes, they bring them (programmes) on when someone has just stopped preaching. Within a quarter of a second nude activities are brought on the screen. It has gone to extremes," he said.
"They bring in little children and start teaching them these dirty dances. We are definitely moving in to stop this rubbish," he added.
This is the second time that the government of President Frederick Chiluba government has tried to censor television.
Five years ago it banned Islamic programmes and popular Zairean musicals but lifted the ban following widespread protests.
President Chiluba in 1991 decreed Zambia "a Christian state tolerant of other religions". Last year, the government pushed through controversial clauses making the decree part of the constitution.
